sections.h2: How can a Denison owner sell quickly?
sections.html:
A Denison seller has three paths: hire an agent to list, find a buyer alone, or sell to a cash purchaser. Speed, repair cost and final price pull against each other, so rank them before you take any call.

Denison is a railroad town. The city's FAQ says it was established on September 23, 1872 and incorporated on March 7, 1873, and that it was named for a Katy Railroad vice president who never came to Texas. It sits in Grayson County and the city puts its population at roughly 28,000. A smaller city means a smaller pool of listing buyers, and houses with deferred maintenance can sit longer than they would in a big metro.

  • On the market: a stronger price is possible, with open houses, inspection requests and loan approval ahead of you.
  • By owner: the commission is yours to keep, along with all contracts and haggling.
  • To a cash buyer: fewer contingencies and a quicker closing, with a price that absorbs the buyer's repair work.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a Denison house, and what does the city list?
sections.html:
The Grayson County Tax Assessor-Collector bills and collects it, and the Grayson County Appraisal District sets the value. The city's tax rates page lists the main office at 100 W Houston in Sherman and a Denison office at the County Sub-Courthouse at 101 W Woodard, and puts the appraisal district at 205 N Travis Street in Sherman.

The same page lists these rates for each $100 of value, under a 2025 tax year heading. Read the table as the city prints it, and ask the county tax office for the rates that apply to your own bill, since they can differ by property.

The page also prints a sales tax rate of 8.25 percent and a hotel and motel tax rate of 7 percent. It adds that the budget for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026 raises $640,617 more from total property taxes than the year before, a 4.3 percent increase, with $624,568 of the revenue coming from new property added to the roll. For general questions, the city's administration offices are at 300 W. Main St., and Main Street and tourism staff work out of the Katy Depot on East Main.

sections.h2: What does a Denison seller owe on the tax bill?
sections.html:
Notices arrive in October, and the Comptroller's page puts the usual payment cutoff at January 31. Taxes still unpaid on February 1 count as delinquent.

After that date the collector adds penalty and interest, and the penalty climbs until July 1. A lien for the year attaches on January 1 to whoever owns the property then, which is why a buyer and a title company want the current year settled at closing.

  • Call the Grayson County tax office early for the balance on your account.
  • Homeowners over 65 or disabled can pay in four installments under state law.
  • Some collectors allow payment plans on delinquent taxes, and a homestead owner can require one.

If back taxes are owed, the balance can come out of the sale money when the title company settles the file.

sections.h2: What does Denison require before I renovate or hand over a house?
sections.html:
Denison's building department issues permits for most structural work, and the city's FAQ lists several that sellers often overlook. A permit is needed for any new fence, a replacement fence, or a repair involving 20 feet or more of fence, and for every detached storage building or shed regardless of size.

A building permit stays valid while work continues, and expires if work is suspended or abandoned for 180 days after it was issued or after the last approved inspection. The FAQ also says a homeowner can pull a homeowner permit for an owner-occupied single-family home only if the property is homestead-exempt as verified through the appraisal district. If it is a rental or not homestead-exempt, the applicant must register as a general contractor and cannot do electrical, plumbing or mechanical work that needs a state license.

A downtown area from the 700 block of West Main to the 300 block of East Main, between Gandy Street and Crawford Street, sends exterior work, including painting, to the Historical Preservation Board. A buyer planning changes there should ask the city first.

sections.h2: What if the Denison house was inherited or the mortgage is behind?
sections.html:
Both situations have fixed steps under Texas law, and a quick sale is possible in either one if the paperwork is ready. For an inherited house, a will has a four-year probate window. When there is no will and the estate is small, the State Law Library describes a small estate affidavit with a $75,000 limit on assets, excluding homestead and exempt property, that a court must approve.

For a mortgage in default, the lender sends a notice of default and you may reinstate by paying the past-due amount within 20 days. The auction notice follows, with the public sale held in a morning-to-afternoon window on a first Tuesday. Ask the Grayson County clerk where foreclosure notices are posted.

Closing before the sale date stops the foreclosure on that loan. Ask your servicer for a payoff statement in writing.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded after a Denison sale?
sections.html:
A notary witnesses the signature, and the Grayson County clerk, who keeps the land records, files the deed. Under the Texas Courts clerk manual, a conveyance without a proper acknowledgment is not eligible for recording.

The title company will quote the clerk's recording charges for your deed. Your title company will quote the final total. A Denison house is filed in Grayson County, the county of the land, even though a branch tax office sits in town.

Before you list, gather the last deed, your tax receipts and any lien releases. A missing document can hold up a closing, and the title company will ask to see each one.

The department's FAQ also describes certificates of occupancy for new buildings and tenant spaces. That rule mainly reaches commercial property, so the owner of a mixed-use building downtown should ask the department which applies. Permit payments in person are taken by cash or check at the Building Inspections office, with cards accepted through the online portal.

faqs.q: Which county handles taxes on a house in Denison?
faqs.a: Grayson County. The county's Tax Assessor-Collector bills the tax and the Grayson County Appraisal District sets the value, per the city's tax rates page.

faqs.q: Does Denison tell homeowners the total tax rate?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's page lists a combined rate of 2.318114 per $100 valuation for the 2025 tax year, built from the city, school district, county and college rates. Ask the county tax office for the figure on your own bill.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for a shed or fence in Denison?
faqs.a: Yes for a shed of any size, and for a new fence or a repair covering 20 feet or more. The city asks for a site plan with dimensions from the property lines.

faqs.q: What date do Texas taxes turn delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1, for taxes not paid by January 31. A six percent penalty and one percent interest are added then.

faqs.q: Is probate always required to sell an inherited Denison house?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A small estate affidavit, a muniment of title or an affidavit of heirship are routes the State Law Library describes, and a title company decides what it will accept. Ask the Grayson County clerk what must be filed.
